v.why: Replacing a skip on the first edge with a 3x3 conv gave +43/+45/+17 in the all-skip parent, versus about 0 when other edges already carry convs.
Upgrading a skip edge to a conv helps a lot in a skip-dominated cell (+35/+32/+11), but is near zero or negative in a conv-rich cell.
Replacing a skip with a conv on edge 1 gave +35/+32/+10 in the all-skip parent, but was slightly negative in parents that already had other convs.
Adding a conv to a missing direct 0→3 edge restores the input-output path when the output is otherwise disconnected (+78/+66/+37).
Filling an absent edge 3 with a skip reconnects the output node and gives large gains (+74/+57/+26), unlike swapping a different existing op.
Adding a conv where edge 4 is absent gives a bigger gain on all three datasets (+6 to +77 in the none-edge parents) than modifying an existing conv.
With edge 4 absent, removing edge 3 cuts the main path to the output and drops accuracy sharply (-74/-56/-27), whereas redundant paths absorb the removal.
If edge 4 is absent, edge 5 is a critical path into node 3, so deleting it is catastrophic (-76/-62/-28) compared with parents that have redundant routes.
With edges 3 and 4 absent, edge 1 is a key link in the only route to the output, so removing it is catastrophic (-76/-62/-28).
Upgrading a skip on the final edge to a conv gave large gains in the all-skip parent (+45/+46/+18), but about zero when other edges already carry convs.

raw:
I've written these from the 100 experiments without running any further tests. Several are only partly supported: the conditions are mostly the same edge, or a "none" in the downstream path that makes the edit decisive, and a few parent cells in the data are counterexamples. The strongest signal is that adding a real operation to an edge that is currently `skip_connect` or `none` gives very large gains when the cell is otherwise weak. The same edit on an edge that already carries a convolution gives near-zero or small gains. Removing an edge is catastrophic when nothing else carries the 0→3 signal.
